first_impression.reaction: Grandmother opener is nice but I'm on the train, I want the list. Key takeaways show up quickly enough so I stayed. Honestly the takeaways read more like a fact-check than an answer though. I wanted 'here are the traditions' and got 'these ones might not be real'.

journey.quote: Portuguese wedding traditions are quieter and more local than most lists suggest, and several customs repeated online have no Portuguese source at all.
journey.reaction: Ok, that's different from the usual listicle. Makes me think this one is actually checked. Good.

journey.quote: The groom's tie, the bride's shoe and the sugared almonds are often told rather than documented, so ask your family which ones they actually keep.
journey.reaction: So... are they traditions or not? I came for the answer and the summary mostly tells me what isn't certain. I'd still like one line that just names the main customs.

journey.quote: Australians marrying legally in Portugal start the process in person at a civil registry office with a certificate of no impediment, and should allow at least a month.
journey.reaction: I'm not Australian and I didn't search for paperwork. Using one of four takeaway slots on this feels off-topic for my query.

journey.quote: When a family talks about choosing the padrinhos, they mean the people who will stand beside the couple and witness the marriage, not a decorative bridal party.
journey.reaction: This is the one section I'd actually read. Clear, short, tells me something I didn't know. Good.

journey.section: The Minho bride in black and Viana gold filigree
journey.quote: One practical detail for brides wearing a family heirloom: traditional Portuguese gold is 19.2 carat.
journey.reaction: Specific and kind of fun. That's the bit I'd screenshot.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Portugal as an Australian
journey.quote: This section is a summary of official sources as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Nice that it's dated, so I know it's current. But this section and the travel notes are long, and on my phone it's a lot of scrolling to reach the FAQ.

journey.quote: The customs with the clearest roots are choosing the padrinhos as witnesses, the enxoval of linen and clothes for married life, and the long copo-d'água feast after the ceremony.
journey.reaction: This is the answer I wanted at the top. It's buried in the FAQ near the bottom.

unanswered_questions: What are the main traditions, in one quick list near the top?
Is the Minho black bridal dress still worn today or only at festivals and museums?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Portuguese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly clickbaity title, and the page doesn't really deliver a 'did not know' list. It's more about what's real and what isn't.

turn_offs_found.quote: The groom's tie is the clearest example. Portuguese-language search results for the custom come almost entirely from Brazilian sites, and one Brazilian bridal magazine calls it Brazilian in origin.
turn_offs_found.why: Interesting, but now it's the second or third time I'm told the tie custom is doubtful. It repeats across sections and adds scrolling.

would_share_with: A friend marrying into a Portuguese family (the padrinhos and gold bits)

cta_reaction.quote: If the paperwork feels like the part that could unravel the plan, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: I just wanted the traditions. I'm not planning anything yet. Not pushy though, so it didn't annoy me. I might click the world traditions guide instead.

top_3_changes: Make the first key takeaway a plain list of the main traditions (padrinhos, enxoval, copo-d'água feast, Minho gold) so the answer to the search is up top, not only in the FAQ.
Swap the Australian legal takeaway for a tradition point, or shorten it, since it doesn't match the search question.
Say once in one place that the tie, shoe and almond customs are unverified, instead of repeating it in the takeaways, the day section, the 'hard to trace' section and the FAQ.
